title: Finite lists of stage module elements vanish at a common later tensor stage
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed partially ordered set, $F:I\to\mathrm{CRing}$ a functor, and $A=\operatorname{colim}_I F$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $i\in I$, an arbitrary $F_i$-module $N$, and a finite subset $s\subset N$. If $1\otimes n=0$ in $A\otimes_{F_i}N$ for every $n\in s$, there exists $j\ge i$ such that $1\otimes n=0$ in $F_j\otimes_{F_i}N$ for every $n\in s$. No generation or presentation assumption on $N$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the eventual-zero clause of TensorProduct.directedColimitBaseChangeElementwise with base stage i to the tensor 1 tensor n at i. Its image is the final unit tensor, hence is zero by the hypothesis. The resulting transition image is the unit tensor at a later stage.

The linear tensor map induced by the stage ring homomorphism sends a unit tensor to the same unit tensor at the later stage and sends zero to zero. Induction on s, combining the singleton stage and the remaining finite set stage at a common upper bound, proves simultaneous vanishing. For the empty set take i.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05LI (1); second reading by V4 realizes the tensor-colimit step with the existing proved directed base-change elementwise theorem, then finite-set induction.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_stage_finite_tensor_vanishing
    {I : Type u} [PartialOrder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat) (i : I) (N : ModuleCat (F.obj i)) (s : Finset N)
    (hs : ∀ n ∈ s,
      (1 : ↑(colimit F)) ⊗ₜ[F.obj i,CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.ι F i)] n = 0) :
    ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j), ∀ n ∈ s,
      (1 : F.obj j) ⊗ₜ[F.obj i,CommRingCat.Hom.hom (F.map (homOfLE hij))] n = 0
